sources.title: NISTIR 8202 Blockchain Technology Overview
sources.readScope: Abstract, Executive Summary, section3.3 asymmetrickey cryptography; scope of ledger/block/consensus concepts
sources.access: public PDF text
sources.limits: 2018 conceptual report. Did not adopt the erroneous private-key encryption analogy in section3.3 or absolute descriptions of every transaction/signature. Signature explanation checked against actual BIP340 algorithm.

sources.title: BIP340 Schnorr Signatures for secp256k1
sources.readScope: Key encodings, implicitY, Public Key Generation and signature Verification
sources.access: public rendered specification
sources.limits: Master document selected sections; no real key or signature generated; public key encodings differ by protocol.

sources.title: Ethereum accounts
sources.readScope: EOA keypairs, account creation, Keccak-based20-byte addresses, contract creation address distinction
sources.access: public official documentation
sources.limits: Do not generalize simplified EOA no-code statement to EIP7702. No CLI examples used.

sources.title: Bitcoin transactions and P2PKH/P2SH conditions
sources.readScope: P2PKH keypair/address/output/signature distinction and P2SH explanation
sources.access: public technical guide
sources.limits: Contains historical Core0.9/P2PKH-dominance description not adopted as current scope; contemporary x-only form checked separately.

sources.title: Web3 Secret Storage V3 definition
sources.readScope: V3 Definition, password/KDF fields, MAC verification, cipher parameters
sources.access: public official format definition
sources.limits: No web3.js/recognizer/API/CLI usage adopted; no real secret, keystore or decryption tested.

sources.title: BIP39: Mnemonic code for generating deterministic keys
sources.readScope: Abstract; Motivation; Generating the mnemonic; Wordlist; From mnemonic to seed; Shortcomings; Related Work. ENT 128-256, ENT/32 checksum, 11-bit indices, 2048-word list, legal word-count table, PBKDF2-HMAC-SHA512 2048 iterations/512-bit seed, UTF-8 NFKD, empty/nonempty passphrase, translation and checksum limits.
sources.access: web open, public rendered primary specification text; lines 212-300
sources.limits: No real mnemonic or passphrase used; no vectors executed in this subtask. Algorithm descriptions checked, implementation interoperability not tested. Existing registry association web-crypto-research-ef670f5fab3d reused for provenance only, not modified.

sources.title: BIP32: Hierarchical Deterministic Wallets
sources.readScope: Abstract; Extended keys; CKDpriv and CKDpub; The key tree; Key identifiers; Serialization format; Master key generation; Compatibility; Security and Implications. Read 32-byte chain code, public derivation boundary, xpub/xprv node scope, metadata/fingerprint limits, parent xpub plus non-hardened descendant private-key leakage warning.
sources.access: web open, public rendered primary specification text; lines 239-392
sources.limits: No actual extended key displayed or derived. Child-key arithmetic is schematic and only explains the specified leakage boundary. Existing registry association web-crypto-research-c613834a37ca reused for provenance only, not modified.

sources.title: BIP44: Multi-Account Hierarchy for Deterministic Wallets
sources.readScope: Path levels, Purpose, Coin type, Account, Change, Index, Account discovery, Address gap limit, Bitcoin mainnet examples. Path roles and apostrophe notation; account/index begin at zero; history rather than current balance; 20-unused-address discovery rule as this specification's rule, not all wallet products.
sources.access: web open, public raw primary specification; GitHub rendered URL first returned Internal Error, raw official repository file read successfully
sources.limits: BIP44 is a path/structure convention, not a claim that all products implement it or that every backup auto-discovers every account. No real wallet scan run.

sources.title: SLIP39: Shamir's Secret-Sharing for Mnemonic Codes
sources.readScope: Abstract; Shamir's secret-sharing; Format of the share mnemonic; relevant Compatibility with BIP-0039 paragraphs. Reviewed different backup/share mechanism, 1024-word 10-bit format, threshold reconstruction, distinction from slicing a BIP39 sentence; not used to prescribe recovery operations.
sources.access: web open/find, public rendered primary specification; selected lines 232-291, 536-548
sources.limits: Only conceptual non-universality and share/reconstruction distinction used. No SLIP39 recovery, checksum implementation or product compatibility test performed.

sources.title: Bitcoin Developer Guide: Wallets
sources.readScope: Introductions; Wallet Programs; Signing-Only Wallets; Offline Wallets; Hardware Wallets. Reviewed separable public-material distribution, signing and network broadcasting, watching-only workflow and hardware communication with networked device.
sources.access: web open, public project documentation; lines 36-101
sources.limits: The page contains dated product-adoption and wallet-format statements; those were not used. Conceptual role separation used only; no CLI/API syntax adopted or hardware security guarantee made.

sources.title: Ethereum wallets: Buy, Store and Send crypto
sources.readScope: What's an Ethereum wallet; Wallets, accounts, keys and addresses; relevant centralized-exchange custody passage. Wallet as application/interface, multiple accounts in one application, exchange custody distinct from username/password access.
sources.access: web open/find; official project documentation redirected from /en/wallets/ to /wallets/; lines 75-112
sources.limits: Simplified identity, absolute transaction irreversibility and only-recovery phrasing on the page were not adopted. Does not independently establish custody classification for a specific MPC product.

sources.title: Ethereum accounts
sources.readScope: Account types; Key differences; Externally-owned accounts and key pairs; A note on wallets. Wallet/account distinction and traditional contract-account authorization by code without a direct private key for the contract address.
sources.access: web open/find; official project documentation redirected from /en/developers/docs/accounts/; selected lines 281-322, 377-379
sources.limits: No account creation tool syntax used. Page's simplified no-code EOA statements were not generalized because delegated-code accounts require network and historical rules. No live contract or account checked.

sources.title: NISTIR 8214: Threshold Schemes for Cryptographic Primitives
sources.readScope: Executive summary, PDF page 6 (printed iv), lines 117-136; Section 3.1.4, PDF page 22 (printed 13), lines 715-743. Secret sharing versus threshold computation without recombining input key; some threshold schemes output a signature indistinguishable from non-threshold signing.
sources.access: web open/find, primary government final report text extraction
sources.limits: Conceptual threshold-signing facts only. No MPC wallet product, custody claim, scheme implementation, security certification or current standardization status asserted; no PDF layout/table/figure claims relied upon.

sources.title: NIST Multi-Party Threshold Cryptography Project
sources.readScope: Overview lines 69-71 and published-report links lines 89-96; confirmed secure MPC-based threshold cryptography covers signatures and found the final NISTIR 8214 report.
sources.access: web open, primary government project overview
sources.limits: Report discovery and conceptual scope only. No current draft/call treated as wallet implementation standard or validation of a particular product.

sources.title: What is a hardware wallet?
sources.readScope: Hardware wallet basics and How do hardware wallets work, selected lines 69-85. Device receives transaction details, signs inside device and returns signature for network broadcast; confirms host-device connection is distinct from raw-secret transfer.
sources.access: web open; primary manufacturer documentation redirected from /learn/a/what-is-a-hardware-wallet
sources.limits: Vendor-specific workflow is corroboration only. Marketing absolutes such as hardware wallets never connect to internet, private key safety on any compromised host, and describing public-key generation as encryption were not adopted. No physical device or firmware tested.

sources.title: Ethereum: Introduction to smart contracts
sources.readScope: What is a smart contract, Permissionless, Composability, Limitations: code/state at address, deployment as transaction, invocation and off-chain data boundary
sources.access: current public primary text; Geth additionally queried through Context7
sources.limits: Did not adopt absolutes about user control, immutable behavior, contract size or universally majority-based multisig.

sources.title: Ethereum accounts
sources.readScope: Account types, fields, keys and wallets: address/account/interface distinction, traditional contract account versus signing account
sources.access: current public primary text; Geth additionally queried through Context7
sources.limits: Historical no-code EOA simplification checked against EIP7702; no live account verified.

sources.title: EIP7702: Set Code for EOAs
sources.readScope: Abstract; specification Behavior and Transaction origination; lines30-120: persistent delegated code, authority nonce, failed execution does not roll back processed delegation
sources.access: current public primary text; Geth additionally queried through Context7
sources.limits: Only applicable to networks and historical protocol rules supporting this transaction type. No authorization signed or broadcast.

sources.title: Ethereum: Technical introduction to dapps
sources.readScope: Definition and On smart contracts, lines281-297: application/frontend/contract roles
sources.access: current public primary text; Geth additionally queried through Context7
sources.limits: Did not adopt claims that all contracts cannot change behavior, all frontends are decentralized, environment never matters or DApps have guaranteed uptime.

sources.title: ERC1967: Proxy Storage Slots
sources.readScope: Abstract/Simple Summary and proxy reference-description paragraphs: implementation address and upgradeable delegation
sources.access: current public primary text; Geth additionally queried through Context7
sources.limits: Conceptual corroboration only; no current library code copied, proxy storage read or deployed code tested.

sources.title: Ethereum transactions
sources.readScope: Transaction fields, lifecycle, gas and contract interaction: request versus inclusion; view/pure simulation versus transaction-path gas
sources.access: current public primary text; Geth additionally queried through Context7
sources.limits: Did not equate block inclusion with successful execution, assume universally fixed gas, or adopt simplified fee-bound formulas.

sources.title: Ethereum gas and fees
sources.readScope: What is gas, lines286-304: resource unit, actual used gas times unit price, fee for failed transactions, native ETH versus gwei
sources.access: current public primary text; Geth additionally queried through Context7
sources.limits: Execution fee formula explicitly separated from blob and L2 other fee components; no fee or price recommendation.

sources.title: Geth eth namespace: eth_call
sources.readScope: Context7 resolve Geth -> /websites/geth_ethereum, query eth_call only; official page eth_call and ephemeral state/block overrides; root direct primary-page read lines533-552
sources.access: current public primary text; Geth additionally queried through Context7
sources.limits: Conceptual simulation distinction only; no request syntax, CLI flags, live node queries, real transactions or simulation runs added. ethereum.org JSONRPC route was inaccessible; not claimed read. Context7 mandatory-block-selector wording, deprecated Rinkeby example and fixed historical retention statement were not adopted.

sources.title: ERC20: Token Standard
sources.readScope: Abstract; optional name/symbol/decimals; balance, transfer and authorization meanings, lines25-102
sources.access: current public primary text; Geth additionally queried through Context7
sources.limits: Historical Solidity signatures not adopted as implementation guidance; decimals is optional and asset identity is not name/symbol.

sources.title: ERC721: Non-Fungible Token Standard
sources.readScope: Abstract; unique token identifiers; ownership interface; optional metadata extension and tokenURI JSON image resource, lines177-215
sources.access: current public primary text; Geth additionally queried through Context7
sources.limits: No claim that metadata/file is always on-chain, permanently immutable or sufficient to establish copyright.

sources.title: ERC1155: Multi Token Standard
sources.readScope: Simple Summary/Abstract and token ID/value distinctions, lines37-69
sources.access: current public primary text; Geth additionally queried through Context7
sources.limits: One contract/id identity separated from quantities; no interface implementation or ERC165-based authenticity assertion.

sources.title: Ethereum oracles
sources.readScope: Introduction, What is a blockchain oracle, Why needed, oracle problem, lines281-318: off-chain feeds and correctness/availability
sources.access: current public primary text; Geth additionally queried through Context7
sources.limits: Consensus acceptance of program input is not proof of real-world truth; no particular oracle product evaluated.

sources.title: IPFS: Content Identifiers
sources.readScope: CID structure, hash/codec/multibase, CIDs are not file hashes, lines49-80
sources.access: current public primary text; Geth additionally queried through Context7
sources.limits: No CLI syntax adopted; CID verification not claimed performed. Integrity is distinct from availability and rights.

sources.title: IPFS: Persistence, permanence and pinning
sources.readScope: Persistence versus permanence, garbage collection, pinning and long-term storage, lines48-86
sources.access: current public primary text; Geth additionally queried through Context7
sources.limits: Pinning retention does not guarantee perpetual service; no pin provider recommendation or availability promise.

entry.intro:
Forensics
/
虚拟币取证
/
基础与证据
虚拟货币与资金流

从助记词、密钥、钱包与合约概念进入区块链原理，再串联设备、链上交易和平台资金流的证据。

基础与证据
专题导航

虚拟币取证先理清助记词、密钥、钱包、账户与智能合约，再掌握区块、共识和账本模型，从设备线索核对钱包与网络，分析链上有效移动、平台记录和资金关系。本页保留聊天、配置、截图、本地账本与笔记历史的资金流核对流程；下列六篇按理论、操作与场景展开。

阅读方向	知识点与考点
基础与证据	基础概念：助记词、密钥、钱包、智能合约；区块链原理与证据流程
钱包与控制权	本地痕迹、派生条件、助记词载体与钱包类型
链上交易	Bitcoin：UTXO、手续费、找零与只读复核；EVM/TRON：回执、代币事件、调用与分页
资金追踪与实战	平台账本、交易图、归因模型、跨链与归属边界；离线账本、区块头与 Merkle 验证、场景考点与报告复核
01 把地址、交易与账本分开验证

资金流取证需要先确认记录的网络、资产、对象和时间范围，再讨论方向与总额。聊天里出现地址支持交流内容，截图支持当时保存的界面图像，本地账本支持应用或人员登记的流水；实际链上交易还需对应网络的交易结构与状态核对。地址存在、交易成功、地址控制权和自然人身份是不同层次的结论。

01.1 常见载体与提取字段
载体	可以提取	交叉材料
聊天记录	地址、转账约定、金额、交易哈希、双方账号与时间	聊天数据库记录 ID、目标网络交易及账户关联
转账截图	界面显示的状态
